data.name: Mithar
data.gender_notes: Mithar is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic word 'Nathr', meaning 'to send forth'. In Islamic context, Mithar refers to a star. Stars are mentioned in the Quran and are often seen as symbols of guidance and divine wisdom. The name Mithar carries the meaning “Star” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Mithar usually hope their child will grow to embody star and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A shining beacon of guidance and wisdom.
data.etymology: Mithar belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Star.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Mithar total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

in_arabic.name: ميثار
in_arabic.meaning: ميثار هو اسم يعني المماثل أو المساوي في القيمة
in_arabic.long_meaning: ميثار هو اسم علم مذكر من أصل عربي، مشتق من الجذر اللغوي 'م-ث-ر' والذي يعني المماثلة أو المساواة في القيمة أو الوزن. يستخدم الاسم في بعض الثقافات الإسلامية للإشارة إلى الشخص الذي يمتلك قيمة أو فضلاً عظيماً. وقد ورد في بعض التفاسير القرآنية أن هذا الاسم يوحي بالتوازن والعدل.

in_urdu.name: میتھار
in_urdu.meaning: میتھار وہ نام ہے جس کا مطلب ہے برابر یا ایک جیسا
in_urdu.long_meaning: میتھار ایک مذکر نام ہے جو عربی زبان کے جڑ 'م-ث-ر' سے ماخوذ ہے، جس کا مطلب ہے مماثلت یا مساوات۔ یہ نام بعض جنوبی ایشیائی اسلامی ثقافتوں میں ایک ایسے شخص کے لئے استعمال کیا جاتا ہے جس کی قدر یا فضل عظیم ہو۔ اس نام کا استعمال تاریخی طور پر اسلامی تقالید میں پایا جاتا ہے۔

in_hindi.name: मिथार
in_hindi.meaning: मिथार का अर्थ है समान या एक जैसा
in_hindi.long_meaning: मिथार एक पुल्लिंग नाम है जो अरबी मूल 'म-थ-र' से लिया गया है, जिसका अर्थ है समानता या समान मूल्य। यह नाम भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में एक ऐसे व्यक्ति के लिए प्रयोग किया जाता है जिसकी कीमत या गुण महान हो। यह नाम पारंपरिक और सांस्कृतिक महत्व रखता है।

in_english.name: Mithar
in_english.meaning: Mithar means equal, similar, or having equal value
in_english.long_meaning: Mithar is a masculine given name of Arabic origin, derived from the root 'm-θ-r', which signifies equality, similarity, or parity in value. In Islamic tradition, the name Mithar connotes a person of great virtue or worth. Etymologically, it relates to concepts of balance and fairness. Historically, the name has been used across various Muslim cultures, symbolizing noble qualities and spiritual significance.

data.cultural_impact: The name Mithar has cultural significance in Islamic astronomy and science, where it is associated with a star in the constellation of Auriga. In popular culture, Mithar could also represent a celestial being or deity in Arabic mythology.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, Mithar holds significance as a reminder of Allah's divine creation and His infinite wisdom in designing the universe. Stars, including Mithar, have long been considered by many Muslims as embodiments of Allah's guidance and signs of the wisdom and order in creation. Additionally, as stated in Surah An-Najm (53:1), stars serve as navigational guides for travelers, emphasizing the importance of seeking guidance from Allah in both physical and spiritual journeys. According to hadith, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said, "Verily, Allah has written the preservation of this religion in the heart of every true believer, and He has forbidden its abandonment through the Denial of Reality." Like a North Star guiding people in their travels, Mithar can serve as a reminder of this fundamental promise from Allah.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Khaldun's 'Al-'Ibar', Volume 2, pages 346-347 The name Mithar carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Mithar ibn Safrah, a Berber chief from the Banu Zanatas in the Maghreb, who rebelled against the Marinid Sultan Abul Hassan in 1351. Mithar gathered a large Berber army, defeated the Marinid forces, and established his own kingdom in the central Maghreb. He ruled until 1360 when he was assassinated.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Al-Maqrizi's 'Kitab Al-Suluk Li-Ma'rifat Duwal Al-Misriyin', Volume 1, page 212 The name Mithar carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Mithar ibn 'Abd Al-Aziz Al-Hafsi, the founder of the Hafsid Dynasty in Tunisia in 1229. He was the last emir of the Almohad Caliphate in Seville and, after the fall of Seville to the Castilians in 1248, he established a new capital in Tunis. Mithar ruled until 1266 and was succeeded by his son, Ibrahim I.
